content:
When Apple finally addressed rising memory and component costs, it took a hard line. Some models have seen price hikes of more than fifty percent, while the cost of upgrading memory and storage on certain configurations has nearly doubled.

These elevated prices are expected to persist for years — and may even become permanent pricing……

9to5Mac readers have long been sceptical about whether Apple will lower prices once the component shortage eases. More than two-thirds of respondents said they expect these price hikes to be permanent.

Subsequently, analyst reports have indicated that supply chain pricing will not see meaningful improvement until at least 2028, and even when conditions ease, any reductions are likely to be quite limited. The current high pricing policy appears set to remain for at least several years — and may never return to previous levels.

If this turns out to be the case, how would you respond? Would you grit your teeth and continue buying Apple products at the same frequency? Or would you cut back on the number or frequency of purchases? Or would you take other approaches, such as opting for cheaper models, buying refurbished units, or waiting until prices drop before making a move?
